title: AniCh Protobuf repeated-field parsing can block the local engine (fixed in this continuation)
description: At the reviewed baseline 95dccdd, repeated fields copied the entire accumulated array for each value. A local fixture containing 100000 empty field-1 records (200000 bytes) took 16007.96 ms in the initial reviewer run; an independent reviewer verified superlinear growth through AniChSource.search at 2000–16000 records. All evidence was local and synthetic. The current working tree replaces copying with push; the same maximum-field-count fixture measured 63.45 ms on Node v24.21.0. This entry records a confirmed, now-remediated issue, not an outstanding vulnerability.
root_cause: decodeFields in packages/engine/src/sources/protobuf.ts at baseline 95dccdd does not append repeated values in place, allowing small valid upstream responses to trigger quadratic synchronous array copying.
intended_behavior: Parse bounded remote AniCh metadata while keeping the shared local API and media engine responsive.

trace.description: Reads the fixed AniCh source response through HttpClient.bytes with the source's URL and signal restrictions.
decodeAniCards invokes protoItems/decodeFields; line 77 also decodes the envelope for its cursor.
Immutable source snapshot from baseline 95dccdd copies the prior array on every repeated field. The live source now appends in place at packages/engine/src/sources/protobuf.ts:37–39.

conditions.description: A configured AniCh upstream response is controlled or compromised; arbitrary unrelated websites cannot select a replacement host.
AniCh is enabled and the user requests search or catalog data that actually fetches the upstream response (a cache miss or explicit refresh).
The baseline parser runs synchronously in the same Node process as the API and media gateway.

execution.attacker_perspective: An actor able to change metadata returned by the configured AniCh upstream, or an equivalent malformed upstream fixture.
payloads: A legal 200000-byte Protobuf buffer containing 100000 empty repeated field-1 records; the isolated regression fixture is in tests/parsers.test.ts.
instructions: Use an isolated in-memory fixture; do not contact a live source.
Feed the bounded response to decodeAniPage or AniChSource.search through a fake HttpClient.
Measure parser duration and a previously scheduled zero-delay timer.
execution.expected_result: On the baseline, synchronous parsing delays the event loop and unrelated local requests; on the fixed tree the same fixture parses in tens of milliseconds on the measured machine.

remediation.strategy: Applied: append to the existing field array, preserving the 100000-field guard and malformed-input checks. Keep the maximum-field regression test.

likelihood.reason: Requires control of a fixed remote source and a user request; no arbitrary-site entry was established.

impact.reason: One small metadata response can temporarily stall the local API and media engine, without data disclosure or persistent modification.

confidence.reason: Independent source tracing and local dynamic measurements confirmed the pre-fix behavior; the current patch and parser regression cover the same bounded input.
